summary: Iteration 8 delta retest of multi-language backend fix. LanguageInput / UserPublic Literal widened to ['en','hi','mr','ta','te','bn']. All 8 tests in test_multilang_i7.py now PASS (previously 4-6 expected to fail for mr/ta/te/bn). Independently verified: POST /api/auth/language returns 200 for each of en,hi,mr,ta,te,bn; returns 422 for 'xx' and 'fr'; GET /api/auth/me after setting 'mr' returns language='mr' (round-trip through UserPublic serialization OK). Frontend loads correctly, language dropdown shows all 6 languages, switching produced 0 console errors and 0 /api/auth/language 422 responses.
critical_code_review_comments: Suggest centralizing the supported language list (currently repeated as Literal in LanguageInput and UserPublic) into a single enum/constant to avoid future drift when adding a 7th language.
seed_data_creation: None persistent; ephemeral test users only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 8 delta (backend Literal widening) fully verified. test_multilang_i7.py now passes 8/8. All previous iteration_6/7 features unaffected — only backend/models.py Literals changed.
rca of the issue: Prior iteration 7: LanguageInput.language and UserPublic.language were Literal['en','hi'] while frontend exposes 6 language buttons — POST /api/auth/language with mr/ta/te/bn was rejected with 422 (silently swallowed on FE). Fix: widened both Literals to include mr,ta,te,bn. Verified backend acceptance, persistence via /me, and rejection of unknown codes still returns 422.
